seoTitle: Fix Shopify Product Showing Sold Out With Stock Left
metaDescription: Shopify product has inventory but still shows Sold Out? Fix location mismatches, variant quantities, and sales channel settings causing the display bug.
intro: It's a common and confusing Shopify problem: your product has stock available, but the storefront still shows it as "Sold Out" or "Unavailable." This usually comes down to inventory settings, fulfillment location mismatches, unpublished sales channels, or a variant with its quantity left at zero rather than an actual stock shortage. This guide walks through the exact admin screens where these mismatches hide, so you can find and fix the real cause instead of guessing.

steps.heading: Confirm the product's real stock in the Products list
steps.body: Start in Products, where the list view shows Status, Inventory, Category, Channels, and Catalogs columns side by side for every item. A product marked Active with "2 in stock" or "35 in stock for 24 variants" clearly has inventory on paper — if the storefront still shows it as sold out, the mismatch is in how that stock is assigned or published, not in whether it exists.

image.caption: The Products list, showing Active items with their in-stock counts, category, channel count, and catalog count in one view.

steps.heading: Open the product and check the Inventory panel
steps.body: Click into the product itself and scroll to the Inventory section. This panel breaks stock down by Locations, with separate columns for Unavailable, Committed, Available, and On hand at each fulfillment location — in a single-location setup you might see a location like "Talborjt" with 2 Available and 2 On hand. If Available reads 0 while On hand shows stock, that gap is usually the direct cause of a sold-out display, since Shopify sells from Available, not from the raw On hand count.

image.caption: The Inventory panel on a product page: Locations, Unavailable, Committed, Available, and On hand columns, plus the "Sell when out of stock" toggle below.

steps.heading: Check "Sell when out of stock" and inventory tracking
steps.body: Just below the Locations table sit the SKU, Barcode, and a "Sell when out of stock" toggle. If Inventory tracked is switched on but the Available count has genuinely hit zero and this toggle is off, Shopify will correctly show the product as sold out — which is expected behavior, not a bug. If the count is wrong rather than zero, the fix is correcting quantities in the next step rather than flipping this toggle.

steps.heading: Fix quantities across variants and locations
steps.body: Products with multiple variants are the most common source of this issue, because a parent product can look fully stocked while individual variants sit at zero. From the variants list, select the affected variants and use Edit quantities to apply a corrected available quantity at the right location in one pass — the dialog shows the location by name and lets you set the same number across every variant you've selected, which is far faster than editing each one individually.

image.caption: The Edit quantities dialog, setting an available quantity at a specific fulfillment location across multiple selected variants at once.

steps.heading: Confirm the product is included in the right catalogs and channels
steps.body: A product can carry correct stock and still appear unavailable if it isn't published everywhere it needs to be. The "Include in catalogs" dialog lists your available catalogs — for example an International catalog alongside a country-specific one like Russia — with checkboxes for which ones include this product. If a customer is browsing through a catalog or market the product isn't checked into, they'll see it as unavailable regardless of how correct the inventory numbers are.

image.caption: The "Include product in catalogs" dialog, with checkboxes for an International catalog and a Russia-specific one.

steps.heading: Rule out theme and dropshipping app conflicts
steps.body: If the admin-side numbers and publishing settings all look correct and the storefront still shows sold out, the cause is likely outside the Shopify admin entirely. Some themes apply their own out-of-stock logic on top of Shopify's inventory data, and dropshipping apps like DSers, Zendrop, or AliExpress periodically sync stock counts from the supplier — a failed sync can silently zero out your Available count. Re-syncing the app or previewing the product with a different theme is the fastest way to isolate which layer is actually causing the display.

steps.heading: Save and verify on the live storefront
steps.body: After adjusting inventory, catalog inclusion, or app sync, save your changes and open the actual product page as a customer would see it rather than trusting the admin view alone. The admin can show "2 in stock" while a caching layer or unsynced theme still displays the old sold-out state for a few minutes, so give it a moment and do a hard refresh before assuming the fix didn't work.

faq.question: Why does my Shopify product show sold out when I have stock?
faq.answer: This is commonly caused by the Available count at a location reading zero even though On hand shows stock, incorrect variant-level quantities, a product missing from the right catalog, or app sync issues rather than an actual lack of stock.

faq.question: Can a dropshipping app cause this sold out display?
faq.answer: Yes — apps like DSers, Zendrop, or AliExpress periodically sync stock counts from the supplier, and a failed sync can zero out your Available quantity even when the supplier actually has stock.

faq.question: Why is only one variant showing out of stock?
faq.answer: This happens when individual variant quantities weren't updated at the right location. Use the Edit quantities dialog to select the affected variants and set a corrected quantity across all of them at once.

faq.question: Does my theme affect whether sold out shows correctly?
faq.answer: Yes — some themes apply their own out-of-stock display logic on top of Shopify's inventory data, which can show a sold-out label even when the admin's Available count is correct.

faq.question: Do I need to republish the product to fix this?
faq.answer: Sometimes — check the "Include in catalogs" dialog to confirm the product is checked into every catalog or market your customers browse through, since a product can be fully in stock and still show unavailable if it's missing from the relevant catalog.
